events.headline: Lamar Jackson limited Wednesday with a back injury; Minter calls it "something small"
events.detail: Jackson was limited in Wednesday's practice with a back issue and was not on the field for the early part of the session before joining later. Head coach Jesse Minter said afterward he is dealing with "something small." Zay Flowers (hamstring) was also limited after playing on a pitch count last week.
events.so_what: A limited tag with a coach downplaying it is a start-him signal, not a sit. Watch Thursday and Friday: a downgrade to DNP would be the real flag, because his rushing floor is the konami premium these leagues pay a QB for. Flowers stays a starter if he is not downgraded.

events.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) DNP Wednesday again; Dallas Goedert (knee) also sits ahead of Rams game
events.detail: Smith was held out of Wednesday's practice, the same routine he followed last week before playing Monday night against the Bears. The Eagles are on a short week hosting the Rams. Goedert (knee) also did not practice and was expected to miss multiple games, so Philadelphia likely plays without its top tight end again.
events.so_what: Smith has played through this exact pattern once already, so treat him as a starter unless Friday brings a designation worse than Questionable. Goedert stays out of lineups.

events.headline: Mason Taylor (thumb) DNP Wednesday, trending toward a second straight absence; Kenyon Sadiq in line for the role again
events.detail: Taylor missed Week 3 with the thumb injury, is considered week-to-week, and did not practice Wednesday. Rookie first-round pick Kenyon Sadiq is coming off a breakout game against the Lions and would again handle the larger share if Taylor sits. Sadiq himself was limited Wednesday with a back injury, per the Jets' report.
events.so_what: Plan on Taylor being out. Sadiq is the streaming tight end in a shallow TE pool if his own back clears by Friday; a second straight start makes his role more than a one-week fill-in.

events.headline: Steelers trade CB Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys for a 2028 second and a conditional sixth
events.detail: Pittsburgh sent Porter, who has not played a snap in 2026 amid a back injury and a contract dispute, to Dallas for a 2028 second-round pick and a conditional 2027 sixth. The Cowboys have been banged up in the secondary and pair him with DaRon Bland. Porter was already ruled out for Thursday night at Cleveland.
events.so_what: Team-defense item only. Dallas's DEF gets a starting corner back once he is healthy, which helps its points-allowed tier; Pittsburgh loses nothing it was using this season.

events.headline: Breece Hall (quad) DNP Wednesday after week-to-week MRI verdict; Braelon Allen lines up to lead vs. Bears
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 28 item. Hall was listed as a non-participant (quad) on the Jets' Wednesday report ahead of Sunday at Chicago. An MRI Monday showed no long-term damage to the right quadriceps and Aaron Glenn calls him week-to-week. Braelon Allen took over the backfield after Hall left in Detroit, with Isaiah Davis also in the mix.
events.so_what: A Wednesday DNP keeps the plan where it was: assume Hall misses Week 4. Allen gets the early-down and goal-line work and is a FLEX start while Hall is out; Davis is a deep handcuff at best.

source.label: New York Jets, Wednesday injury report, Sept. 30

events.headline: Jayden Reed needs season-ending neck surgery, LaFleur confirms
events.detail: Matt LaFleur said Wednesday that Reed will have surgery on the neck he injured in the Week 2 win over the Jets, when he left on a spine board and spent the night in a New Jersey hospital. It ends his 2026 season. LaFleur said he does not believe the injury is career-threatening. Green Bay was expected to place him on IR Wednesday.
events.so_what: Drop him unless the roster has an open IR slot and nothing better to put there. His snaps go to the rest of the Green Bay receiver room, but no single replacement has been named.

events.headline: Tony Pollard (foot) and Tyjae Spears (ankle) both DNP Wednesday; Saleh "not overly concerned" for Sunday
events.detail: Both Titans backs sat out Wednesday practice ahead of the Week 4 game against Baltimore. Both played through the same injuries last week, and Robert Saleh said he is not overly concerned about either being available Sunday.
events.so_what: Coach optimism on two backs who both played last week, but neither is cleared. Keep starting whichever one your lineup uses and check Friday; a Friday downgrade for one would push the other toward most of the work.

events.headline: Chris Godwin pops up with an ankle injury, DNP Wednesday before Week 4 vs. Packers
events.detail: Godwin was a new addition to the Buccaneers injury report Wednesday with an ankle issue and did not practice. He has 10 catches for 111 yards on 11 targets through three games. Tampa Bay is also without Baker Mayfield (thumb) for at least three games, with rookie Jalon Daniels starting, and Jalen McMillan went to IR.
events.so_what: A new injury on a receiver who was already producing little, now catching passes from a rookie. Treat him as a bench unless he practices fully by Friday.

events.headline: Jaylen Wright returns to Dolphins practice limited; Hafley describes a split with Ollie Gordon
events.detail: Wright (stinger, foot) practiced on a limited basis Wednesday, his first work since the injury. Jeff Hafley said the running back work behind the departed De'Von Achane will be split between Wright and Ollie Gordon depending on the play. Wright was the RB2 through camp and ahead of Gordon on the depth chart; Gordon took every running back snap in Week 3 after Achane tore his ACL, with 17 carries for 41 yards and a touchdown.
events.so_what: Wright's return turns Gordon's Week 3 monopoly into a committee. Gordon still looks like the early-down and goal-line back, which is where the TD value is, but neither should be started as a locked RB2 until one of them wins the snaps in a game.

events.headline: Steelers rule Rico Dowdle out for Thursday night at Cleveland
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 29 item. Dowdle (toe) did not practice at all this week and Pittsburgh ruled him out Wednesday for the Thursday night game against the Browns, his second straight missed game. In Week 3 without him Jaylen Warren played 90% of the snaps and ran 17 times for 127 yards with three catches for 31 yards. CB Joey Porter Jr. is also out.
events.so_what: Settled before Thursday kickoff: bench Dowdle and start Warren at RB or FLEX as a near-every-down back again. Dowdle stays a bench hold; nothing points to IR.

events.headline: Justin Jefferson sits out Wednesday practice, day-to-day with the ankle sprain
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 28 item. Kevin O'Connell said Jefferson (ankle sprain, nothing long-term per Monday's MRI) would not practice Wednesday and is day-to-day, adding that he "feels better" after leaving the Week 3 win over Tampa Bay in the first quarter. Minnesota hosts Miami on Sunday.
events.so_what: A Wednesday DNP on a sprain is normal and does not change the outlook, but it is not a clearance. Thursday and Friday participation decide it; keep a WR or FLEX fallback until then.

events.headline: Mike Evans (ribs) sits out Wednesday; Shanahan hopes he practices by the end of the week
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 28 item. Kyle Shanahan said Evans would not practice Wednesday, and told The Athletic he "may" practice later in the week. Evans left the win over Arizona after a hit from Budda Baker; Monday's exam found no significant rib injury. He is also managing a hip that made him Questionable in Week 3.
events.so_what: Still a pain-tolerance question with no practice yet. If he does not practice by Friday, treat him as a bench and play the fallback.

events.headline: Jayden Daniels limited in London jog-through; Quinn has not ruled him out for Week 4
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 28 item. Daniels (dislocated left elbow) was listed as limited in Wednesday's jog-through in London, his first practice since the Week 2 injury. Dan Quinn called it a "good step," said Washington has not ruled him out against the Colts, and confirmed he will wear a brace on the left elbow for the rest of the season whenever he returns. Marcus Mariota threw three touchdowns in the Week 3 upset of Seattle.
events.so_what: Progress, not a clearance. A jog-through limited tag says little about game readiness; watch Thursday and Friday. Until he is confirmed active, a roster leaning on him needs a Week 4 quarterback, and whether the brace changes how often he runs (the konami part of his value) is the thing to watch in his first game back.

events.headline: Nico Collins returns to Texans practice ahead of Week 4 vs. Cowboys
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 28 item. Collins (Grade 1 hamstring) practiced Wednesday for the first time since the injury two weeks ago. He has missed two games and Houston scored 23 points combined in them, against 31 with him in the opener. DeMeco Ryans said Monday the team was hopeful he plays Sunday. In Week 2 without him Dalton Schultz caught 12 of 14 targets for 140 yards.
events.so_what: The practice step that was needed. Lean toward starting him against Dallas, and confirm on Friday's report. If he returns, Schultz goes back to a secondary option and Xavier Hutchinson loses most of his volume.

events.headline: Puka Nacua limited in first practice in two weeks; McVay expects him to play at Philadelphia
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 28 item. Nacua (hip/groin) practiced on a limited basis Wednesday, his first session in nearly two weeks after missing two games, and Sean McVay said he expects him to play Sunday against the Eagles. TE Terrance Ferguson, who drew 29% of the targets in Week 2 without Nacua, is likely out with an ankle sprain.
events.so_what: The strongest signal yet, but still a forecast until Friday's designation. Plan to start him; with Ferguson likely out, the targets concentrate on Nacua and Davante Adams. Keep a WR fallback until the final report.

events.headline: Jalen Coker (quad) and Xavier Legette (knee) both DNP Wednesday; Legette week-to-week
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 28 item. Coker, who left the loss to Cleveland with what was called a minor quad strain while already playing through an ankle, did not practice Wednesday. Xavier Legette (knee) also sat out and Dave Canales called him week-to-week. Carolina promoted WR David Moore from the practice squad.
events.so_what: Two Carolina receivers out of Wednesday practice. Coker needs to practice by Friday to be a usable FLEX against Detroit; bench him until he does. Legette is a bench or drop for now.

events.headline: Buccaneers place Jalen McMillan on injured reserve after he re-injured his left knee
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 27 item. Tampa Bay moved McMillan to IR on Wednesday, so he misses at least the next four games. He re-injured the same left knee that cost him most of camp in the first quarter against Minnesota. Tez Johnson and rookie Ted Hurst are the candidates for his snaps, and Chris Godwin (ankle) also missed Wednesday practice.
events.so_what: An IR stash only if the roster has an open IR slot; otherwise a drop. Tez Johnson is the speculative add, but with Baker Mayfield out and a rookie at quarterback the passing game around him is thin.

events.headline: Caleb Williams misses Wednesday walkthrough; Ben Johnson says Week 4 QB "direction has already been made"
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 27 item. Williams (Grade 2 hamstring, 3-4 week timeline per ESPN) did not take part in Wednesday's walkthrough, and Ben Johnson said he is "getting better every single day." Johnson told 670 The Score the decision on a Week 4 starter against the Jets had been made but did not say whether it is Case Keenum, who threw two TDs and ran for a third in Monday's 27-7 win over the Eagles, or Tyson Bagent.
events.so_what: Plan on Williams missing Week 4 at minimum; hold him rather than drop. Keenum is a streaming option only if he is confirmed as the starter, and even then a low-ceiling one.

events.headline: Giants release Odell Beckham after three games and 19 snaps; sign Braxton Berrios and Charlie Jones
events.detail: New York cut Beckham on Tuesday after he played 19 offensive snaps across three games, and added WRs Braxton Berrios and Charlie Jones to the active roster. Same day the Giants moved J.J. McCarthy to No. 18 after acquiring him from Minnesota.
events.so_what: No fantasy value lost: Beckham had no role. The signings are depth, not a target shift, so nothing changes for the Giants receivers anyone starts.

events.headline: Giants acquire J.J. McCarthy from the Vikings for a 2027 fifth; Jameis Winston stays the starter
events.detail: The Vikings announced Monday that they traded McCarthy to New York for a 2027 fifth-round pick, pending a physical. The Giants lost Jaxson Dart for the season to knee surgery (MCL, PCL and meniscus) in Week 2. John Harbaugh said Monday that Winston remains the starter with McCarthy on the roster, so McCarthy begins as the backup.
events.so_what: No immediate lineup change: Winston keeps the job, and with it the higher-volume, higher-interception passing that feeds Malik Nabers. McCarthy is a watch-list name only if Winston struggles; he is not a stash in a one-QB lineup.

events.headline: Baker Mayfield MRI shows no ligament damage, but Bowles says he misses at least three games; rookie Jalon Daniels starts vs. Packers
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 27 item. Monday's MRI on Mayfield's dislocated right (throwing) thumb found no fracture, tendon or ligament damage, per Ian Rapoport and Jeremy Fowler. Todd Bowles still said Mayfield will miss at least the next three games because the thumb limits his grip, and Mayfield is getting a second opinion before a formal timeline. Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels, who finished Sunday's 23-16 loss to Minnesota, is in line for his first start at home against Green Bay.
events.so_what: Plan on no Mayfield through roughly Week 6, with the second opinion the only thing that could shorten it. A rookie UDFA starter lowers the ceiling of every Tampa Bay pass catcher and tilts the offense toward the run. Do not start Daniels in a one-QB lineup; anyone relying on Mayfield needs a streamer for the next three weeks.

events.headline: De'Von Achane tears his left ACL, out for the season; Hafley says Dolphins backs will all 'have their roles'
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 27 item. Monday's MRI confirmed a torn left ACL, and ESPN reports Achane will miss the rest of 2026. He was hurt in the first quarter of the loss at Kansas City. Ollie Gordon, the only other active back Sunday, finished with 17 carries for 41 yards and a touchdown plus three catches for 14 yards, and receiver Malik Washington took some snaps at running back. Jeff Hafley said Monday that 'they're all going to have their roles,' called Jaylen Wright (stinger, foot) day-to-day, and said he and the GM will discuss adding a back this week.
events.so_what: Achane is a drop-or-IR decision now, not a hold. Gordon is the immediate early-down and goal-line back and the top Miami add, but Hafley's committee language plus a healthy Wright, or a signed veteran, caps him short of the every-down role Achane had. Bid on Gordon as a FLEX with RB2 upside, not as a like-for-like replacement.

events.headline: Travis Etienne will miss time with his hamstring, Kellen Moore says; timetable TBD
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 27 item. Moore said Monday that Etienne will miss time after re-aggravating the left hamstring that limited him in practice Wednesday and Thursday. He left midway through the third quarter of the 35-27 loss to the Raiders after 13 carries for 57 yards. No timetable has been given, so injured reserve has not been ruled in or out.
events.so_what: Plan on at least Week 4 without him, and a recurring hamstring can stretch longer. Alvin Kamara is the likely early-down beneficiary; check which of Kamara, CJ Donaldson and Kendre Miller is on your wire before Tuesday bids.

events.headline: Terrance Ferguson likely out Week 4 with a medial ankle sprain; Colby Parkinson uncertain with an AC sprain
events.detail: McVay said Monday Ferguson re-injured the ankle in the first quarter at Denver, returned for two snaps and left again after his only catch, and is likely to miss Sunday at Philadelphia. Fellow TE Colby Parkinson suffered an AC shoulder sprain in the same game; McVay said "we'll see" on his Week 4 availability.
events.so_what: Ferguson is a bench or drop for Week 4 at a position where the leagues start only one TE. With both Rams tight ends hurt, neither is a streaming answer this week; look elsewhere for a one-week TE.

events.headline: Commanders re-sign Austin Ekeler for depth; Rachaad White played through a shoulder injury
events.detail: Washington is signing Ekeler, pending a physical, back from the Achilles tear that ended his 2025 in Week 2. Team sources say the move was decided Saturday and is unrelated to Rachaad White's shoulder injury, which he suffered in the first half against Seattle before returning. The backfield is White (third downs, 151 scrimmage yards), Jacory Croskey-Merritt (team-high 142 rushing yards) and rookie Kaytron Allen.
events.so_what: Depth signing, not a role change: nobody in this backfield loses a lineup spot today. It does make the Washington committee even harder to start with confidence, and White's shoulder is the item to watch on the Wednesday report.
